finding.claim: Any authenticated user who is not the owner or a listed editor can overwrite the body of any document via PUT /doc/<doc_id>, because the return value of can_edit() is discarded and never enforced.
finding.source: request.json["body"] (docs.py:20) and the doc_id URL parameter, sent by any logged-in caller
finding.sink: doc["body"] assignment at docs.py:20 (document content write)

trace.note: update_doc route registered for PUT /doc/<doc_id> with no authorization decorator
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads the target document
can_edit(g.user, doc) called but its boolean result is discarded; no if/abort/require_edit wraps it

returns {"ok": true}, confirming the write to the caller

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is logically correct but unenforced on this path; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) would abort 403 but is not called in update_doc; no authorization middleware or before_request hook exists in docs.py (not verifiable beyond this file, since the directory contains only docs.py)

verdict.guard_found: none. can_edit at docs.py:7-8 returns a bool that line 19 discards as a bare statement; require_edit (docs.py:11-13, aborts 403) is not called in update_doc; no decorator on the route at docs.py:16; no before_request hook. verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, so its result is never tested, and docs.py:20 writes request.json["body"] into doc["body"] unconditionally. Any authenticated user who reaches PUT /doc/<doc_id> can therefore overwrite any document body; the attacker only needs to be logged in (g.user is set outside this file), which is a low-privilege role.
